segments.text: Welcome back to the Async Work podcast. Today I'm joined by Dr. Ian Mercer, who studies how remote teams make decisions.
Thanks for having me, Nadia. It's a topic I could talk about all day.
Let's start with the big question. Why do remote teams end up with so many meetings, when remote work was supposed to give us more focus time?

In our research, the main reason is uncertainty. When people can't see each other, they schedule a meeting to make sure everyone is aligned. A meeting feels safer than a written proposal, even when a document would be faster.
So what do the best teams do differently?

They separate discussion from decision. Discussion happens in writing over a day or two, and the meeting is only used to make the final call. Those teams had forty percent fewer meetings and made decisions faster.
What about recording meetings and generating summaries with AI? Does that help, or does it just create more content nobody reads?

It helps when the summary is short and the action items are clear. People who miss a meeting can catch up in two minutes instead of watching an hour of video. The key is that someone owns each action item.
If a listener wants to try one thing this week, what should it be?
Pick your most frequent recurring meeting and cancel it for two weeks. Replace it with a written update and see what breaks. Usually nothing does.
Great advice. I'll put a link to your research paper in the show notes. Listeners, please send us your questions about async work by Friday for our next episode.
